question: Who among the following is known as a pioneering dance educationist and a prominent Mohiniyattam exponent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dr Kanak Rele.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Kanak Rele was a pioneering dance educationist and a prominent exponent and reviver of Mohiniyattam, the classical dance form of Kerala. (मोहिनीअट्टम — डॉ. कनक रेले)

 

• She founded the Nalanda Dance Research Centre in Mumbai in 1966, which became a major institution for the study and revival of Mohiniyattam.

 

• She is credited with giving Mohiniyattam a structured and codified technique, similar to other classical dance forms, and received the Padma Shri (1990) for her contribution to dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mohiniyattam is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, characterised by graceful, swaying (lasya) movements, and is closely associated with Kerala.

 

• Other notable classical dance exponents include Madhavi Mudgal (Odissi).

 

NOTE

 

• Madhavi Mudgal (Option 1): She is a renowned exponent of Odissi, not Mohiniyattam.

 

• Shagun Butani (Option 2): Not associated with pioneering Mohiniyattam education.

 

• Mohanrao Kallianpurkar (Option 3): He was a noted scholar and exponent of Kathak, not Mohiniyattam.

question: According to Mendeleev's periodic table, what was the atomic mass of Eka-aluminium which was later replaced by Gallium?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 68.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dmitri Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table for undiscovered elements and predicted their properties; one such gap he named Eka-aluminium. (एका-एल्युमिनियम — गैलियम)

 

• Mendeleev predicted Eka-aluminium would have an atomic mass of about 68 and other properties similar to aluminium.

 

• In 1875, French chemist Paul Émile Lecoq de Boisbaudran discovered the element Gallium, whose properties closely matched Mendeleev's predictions for Eka-aluminium, confirming the predictive power of the periodic table.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mendeleev similarly predicted Eka-boron (later found to be Scandium) and Eka-silicon (later found to be Germanium).

 

• The actual atomic mass of Gallium is about 69.7, very close to Mendeleev's predicted value of 68.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (95, 83, 50): These do not match Mendeleev's predicted atomic mass of approximately 68 for Eka-aluminium.

question: What is the outermost layer found in the cell envelope of the bacterial cell called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Glycocalyx.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The glycocalyx is the outermost, viscous layer of the bacterial cell envelope, lying external to the cell wall. (ग्लाइकोकैलिक्स — जीवाणु कोशिका की सबसे बाहरी परत)

 

• It is composed of polysaccharides (and sometimes proteins) and exists in two main forms: a well-organised capsule or a diffuse, unorganised slime layer.

 

• The glycocalyx helps bacteria in adhesion to surfaces, protection from desiccation and phagocytosis, and in some cases contributes to virulence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The general bacterial cell envelope, from outside to inside, is: Glycocalyx → Cell wall → Plasma (cell) membrane → Cytoplasm.

 

• The cell wall, made largely of peptidoglycan, lies just beneath the glycocalyx and provides structural rigidity.

 

NOTE

 

• Cell membrane / Plasma membrane (Options 2 and 3): These are the innermost, selectively permeable membranes enclosing the cytoplasm, not the outermost layer.

 

• Cytoplasm (Option 4): This is the gel-like internal content of the cell, well within the cell envelope, not an outer layer at all.

question: Which of the following Indian classical dance forms uses various colours on face to symbolise the characters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form from Kerala known for its elaborate makeup called "Vesham", where different colours symbolise different character types. (कथकली — केरल का शास्त्रीय नृत्य)

 

• In Kathakali makeup, green (Pacha) denotes noble/heroic characters, red (Kathi) denotes villainous characters, black is used for demons/hunters, and white beard/features denote celestial beings.

 

• The elaborate costumes, headgear and face painting allow the audience to instantly identify the nature of each character even without dialogue, as Kathakali relies heavily on Mudras (hand gestures) and facial expressions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kathakali draws its themes mainly from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and Puranas.

 

• Other classical dance forms of India include Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Odissi (Odisha), Kathak (North India), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam), and Mohiniyattam (Kerala).

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 1): A classical dance form of Odisha, characterised by fluid, sculpturesque body movements (Tribhangi), not elaborate face-colour makeup.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 3): A classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, uses expressive eye and hand movements (Abhinaya), not symbolic face colours.

 

• Mohiniattam (Option 4): A graceful, lyrical dance form of Kerala performed mainly by women, without the elaborate coloured facial makeup used in Kathakali.

question: President Droupadi Murmu has appointed Dr. Justice Dhananjaya Yashwant Chandrachud as the _______ Chief Justice of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 50th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Justice D. Y. Chandrachud was appointed as the 50th Chief Justice of India, taking oath on 9 November 2022, administered by President Droupadi Murmu. (मुख्य न्यायाधीश — डॉ. डी. वाई. चंद्रचूड़, 50वें)

 

• He succeeded Justice Uday Umesh Lalit (49th CJI) and served until his retirement on 10 November 2024.

 

• Justice Chandrachud is the son of Justice Y. V. Chandrachud, who was the longest-serving Chief Justice of India (16th CJI).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Droupadi Murmu became the 15th President of India, taking office on 25 July 2022.

 

• Justice D. Y. Chandrachud was succeeded as CJI by Justice Sanjiv Khanna (51st CJI).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (51st): This refers to Justice Sanjiv Khanna, Chandrachud's successor, not Chandrachud himself.

 

• Options 3 and 4 (48th, 49th): The 48th CJI was N. V. Ramana and the 49th CJI was U. U. Lalit — both predecessors of Justice Chandrachud.

question: Which Part of the Constitution of India reflects the Fundamental Duties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part IV-A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fundamental Duties of citizens are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Constitution, under Article 51-A. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — भाग IV-A)

 

• Part IV-A was added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

• Originally, there were 10 Fundamental Duties; a 11th duty (regarding the duty of parents/guardians to provide education to their children/wards) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Soviet Union).

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., not enforceable by courts.

 

NOTE

 

• Part X (Option 1): Deals with the Scheduled and Tribal Areas.

 

• Part XII (Option 2): Deals with Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits.

 

• Part IX-B (Option 4): Deals with Co-operative Societies, added by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011.

question: When did the Mongol ruler Genghis Khan die?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1227.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Genghis Khan, the founder and first Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, died in August 1227, during a military campaign against the Western Xia. (चंगेज़ खान — मंगोल साम्राज्य)

 

• He united the Mongol and Turkic tribes of Central Asia and went on to found the largest contiguous land empire in history.

 

• After his death, the empire was divided among his sons and grandsons, eventually leading to Khanates such as the Yuan Dynasty in China founded by his grandson Kublai Khan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Genghis Khan was born around 1162 with the birth name Temüjin.

 

• The exact location of his burial remains unknown to this day.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (1219, 1210, 1235): These years do not correspond to Genghis Khan's death; 1219 marks the start of his invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire, while 1235 falls after his death, during the reign of his successor Ögedei Khan.

question: How many maximum electrons can M shell have?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in a shell is given by the formula 2n², where n is the shell number. (कोश की अधिकतम इलेक्ट्रॉन क्षमता — 2n²)

 

• The M shell is the third shell from the nucleus, i.e., n = 3, so its maximum capacity is 2 × 3² = 2 × 9 = 18 electrons.

 

• The shells are named K (n=1), L (n=2), M (n=3), N (n=4), and so on, with maximum capacities of 2, 8, 18, and 32 electrons respectively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• This electron-shell filling model was proposed by Niels Bohr as part of the Bohr model of the atom.

 

• The outermost shell of an atom, called the valence shell, determines many of its chemical properties.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 (8): This is the maximum capacity of the L shell (n=2), not the M shell.

 

• Option 3 (1): Does not correspond to any shell's maximum capacity under the 2n² rule.

 

• Option 4 (2): This is the maximum capacity of the K shell (n=1), not the M shell.

question: Merchants and migrants first brought the teachings of the holy Quran to India in the ______ century.
solution_text:
The correct answer is seventh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arab merchants and migrants first brought the teachings of the Holy Quran and Islam to India, particularly along the Malabar (Kerala) coast, in the 7th century CE. (कुरान की शिक्षाएँ — 7वीं शताब्दी)

 

• This early contact was largely peaceful, driven by the flourishing Arab trade with the Malabar coast even before the advent of Islam.

 

• The first organised military expansion of Islam into the Indian subcontinent came later, with Muhammad bin Qasim's conquest of Sindh in 712 CE, also in the 7th–8th century timeframe.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Cheraman Juma Masjid in Kerala, traditionally dated to 629 CE, is often cited as one of the earliest mosques in India, reflecting this early Arab contact.

 

• Islam later spread more widely in India through the Delhi Sultanate (from the 13th century) and the Mughal Empire.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (fourth, ninth, sixth centuries): These do not match the historically accepted 7th-century timeframe for the first arrival of Quranic teachings via Arab merchants and migrants.

question: In 1955, which synthetic element is provisionally named Mendelevium in honor of Dmitri Mendeleev, who created one of the first periodic tables?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Element 101.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mendelevium (symbol Md, atomic number 101) was first synthesised in 1955 by a team at the University of California, Berkeley, led by Albert Ghiorso and Glenn T. Seaborg. (मेंडेलीवियम — तत्व संख्या 101)

 

• It was named in honour of Dmitri Mendeleev, the Russian chemist who devised the periodic table and pioneered the method of predicting properties of undiscovered elements.

 

• Mendelevium was notable for being synthesised one atom at a time, making it the first element produced by this technique.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mendelevium is a member of the actinide series and is highly radioactive, with no known uses outside of scientific research.

 

• Other elements named after scientists include Curium (96, Marie/Pierre Curie) and Einsteinium (99, Albert Einstein).

 

NOTE

 

• Element 90 (Option 1): This is Thorium, named after the Norse god Thor.

 

• Element 103 (Option 3): This is Lawrencium, named after Ernest Lawrence.

 

• Element 106 (Option 4): This is Seaborgium, named after Glenn T. Seaborg himself, one of Mendelevium's discoverers.

question: In Trans – Siberian railway system Vladivostoclies on ______ coast.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pacific.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vladivostok, the eastern terminus of the Trans-Siberian Railway, lies on the Pacific coast of Russia, on the Sea of Japan. (व्लादिवोस्तोक — प्रशांत महासागर तट)

 

• The Trans-Siberian Railway connects Moscow in the west to Vladivostok in the Russian Far East, spanning roughly 9,289 km, making it the longest railway line in the world.

 

• It passes through major cities including Yekaterinburg, Omsk, Novosibirsk, Irkutsk, and runs along Lake Baikal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Construction of the Trans-Siberian Railway began in 1891 and was largely completed by 1916.

 

• Vladivostok is also home to Russia's Pacific Fleet naval base.

 

NOTE

 

• Atlantic (Option 1): Vladivostok does not lie on the Atlantic coast; the Atlantic borders western Russia via the Baltic and Black Seas, far from Vladivostok.

 

• Antarctic (Option 2) and Arctic (Option 3): Vladivostok does not lie on the Antarctic or Arctic coasts; Russia's Arctic coastline lies far to the north.

question: The crop area under high yielding varieties of which amongst the following crop grew considerably during the Green Revolution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wheat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution, launched in India in the mid-1960s under the guidance of M. S. Swaminathan, led to a dramatic expansion of area under High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, most prominently for wheat. (हरित क्रांति — गेहूं)

 

• Norman Borlaug's semi-dwarf, high-yielding wheat varieties were adapted for Indian conditions and led to a sharp jump in wheat production, especially in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

• This period made India self-sufficient in food grains, transforming it from a food-deficit to a food-surplus nation for wheat and rice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rice was the other major crop that saw a significant HYV-driven expansion, though wheat's growth was the most dramatic.

 

• Crops like pulses and oilseeds largely remained outside the ambit of the Green Revolution and continued to show relatively low yield growth — often called the "neglected crops" of the Green Revolution.

 

NOTE

 

• Sugarcane (Option 1): Not a primary focus crop of the Green Revolution's HYV expansion.

 

• Pulses (Option 2) and Oilseeds (Option 3): These crops saw comparatively little benefit from Green Revolution technologies and are often cited as the sectors it largely bypassed.

question: Who has become the 12th Chief minister of Uttarakhand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pushkar Singh Dhami.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pushkar Singh Dhami took oath as the 12th Chief Minister of Uttarakhand on 23 March 2022, after leading the BJP to victory in the 2022 Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly elections. (पुष्कर सिंह धामी — उत्तराखंड के मुख्यमंत्री)

 

• He had earlier served as the 11th Chief Minister from July 2021 to March 2022, having been appointed after Tirath Singh Rawat resigned.

 

• Under Dhami's leadership, the BJP retained power in Uttarakhand for a second consecutive term, a rare feat in the state's political history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uttarakhand was carved out of Uttar Pradesh as a separate state on 9 November 2000.

 

• Uttarakhand's capital is Dehradun (interim capital), with Gairsain designated as the summer capital.

 

NOTE

 

• Biren Singh (Option 1): He is the Chief Minister of Manipur, not Uttarakhand.

 

• Pramod Sawant (Option 2): He is the Chief Minister of Goa, not Uttarakhand.

 

• Bhagwant Singh Mann (Option 3): He is the Chief Minister of Punjab, not Uttarakhand.

question:
Which of the following statement is correct?

I. The nutrition requirements of adolescents are higher than adult.

II. Adolescents are generally grouped in the age group of 10 to 19 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are correct. Adolescence is a period of rapid physical growth and development, requiring greater nutritional intake than adulthood. (किशोरावस्था — 10 से 19 वर्ष)

 

• Statement I is correct: During adolescence, the body undergoes a growth spurt, along with hormonal and physiological changes, which increases the requirement for energy, protein, iron, calcium and other micronutrients compared to adults.

 

• Statement II is correct: As per the World Health Organization (WHO), adolescents are defined as individuals in the 10 to 19 years age group.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The WHO further classifies youth as the 15–24 years age group and young people as the 10–24 years age group.

 

• Adolescence is typically divided into early (10–13 years), middle (14–16 years) and late (17–19 years) stages.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (Only II / Neither / Only I): These are incorrect because each of them wrongly rejects at least one of the two factually correct statements.

question: Which Article of the Constitution separates the judiciary from the executive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 50.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 50 of the Indian Constitution, a Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP), directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State. (अनुच्छेद 50 — न्यायपालिका का कार्यपालिका से पृथक्करण)

 

• This provision aims to ensure the independence of the judiciary by preventing the executive from controlling judicial functions.

 

• Article 50 falls under Part IV of the Constitution, which deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy and is non-justiciable in nature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Directive Principles of State Policy are inspired by the Irish Constitution and are contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51).

 

• The independence of the judiciary is also reinforced by provisions relating to the appointment, tenure and removal of judges under Articles 124 and 217.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 143 (Option 1): Deals with the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

 

• Article 144 (Option 3): Requires civil and judicial authorities to act in aid of the Supreme Court.

 

• Article 74 (Option 4): Provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President.

question: What do you call a component of identical size that offers a higher resistance to electricity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poor conductor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A poor conductor is a material that, for a given size/dimension, offers higher resistance to the flow of electric current, allowing only a small amount of current to pass. (कुचालक — उच्च प्रतिरोध)

 

• Electrical resistance depends on the material's resistivity, along with its length and cross-sectional area; materials with high resistivity are classified as poor conductors.

 

• Common examples of poor conductors include rubber, wood, glass and mica, which are often used as insulators.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Materials are broadly classified as conductors (low resistance, e.g., copper, silver), semiconductors (intermediate, e.g., silicon, germanium), and insulators/poor conductors (very high resistance).

 

• Silver is the best known conductor of electricity, followed closely by copper, which is used widely in wiring due to its lower cost.

 

NOTE

 

• Semi-conductor (Option 2): Offers intermediate resistance, between conductors and insulators — not the highest resistance.

 

• Good conductor (Option 3) and Very good conductor (Option 4): These offer low resistance, allowing current to pass easily, the opposite of what the question describes.

question: In which of the following months did the Australian Open take place in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is January.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Australian Open, a Grand Slam tennis tournament, was held at Melbourne Park from 17 to 30 January 2022. (ऑस्ट्रेलियन ओपन 2022 — जनवरी)

 

• The men's singles title was won by Rafael Nadal, who defeated Daniil Medvedev in a five-set final, completing his record-setting 21st Grand Slam title at the time.

 

• The women's singles title was won by Ashleigh Barty of Australia, who defeated Danielle Collins in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Australian Open is traditionally the first Grand Slam of the tennis calendar year, held every January.

 

• The other three Grand Slams are the French Open (Roland Garros), Wimbledon, and the US Open.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (February, March, April): The Australian Open is not held in these months; it is traditionally held in January each year.

question: Which of the following is celebrated as the "Tibetan New Year"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Losar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Losar is celebrated as the Tibetan New Year, marking the beginning of the year according to the Tibetan lunar calendar. (लोसार — तिब्बती नव वर्ष)

 

• It is celebrated over several days with prayers, traditional dances, family gatherings, and rituals to ward off evil spirits from the past year.

 

• Losar is widely celebrated by Tibetan Buddhist communities in regions such as Tibet, Sikkim, Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh (Tawang), and by the Tibetan diaspora in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Myoko is a festival celebrated by the Apatani tribe of Arunachal Pradesh.

 

• Other regional New Year festivals in India include Ugadi (Andhra Pradesh/Telangana), Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), and Baisakhi (Punjab).

 

NOTE

 

• Lohang (Option 1): Not a recognised name for the Tibetan New Year.

 

• Myoko (Option 3): A festival of the Apatani tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, unrelated to the Tibetan New Year.

 

• Murung (Option 4): A festival celebrated by the Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, not the Tibetan New Year.

question: Which layer of atmosphere helps in radio transmission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thermosphere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Thermosphere contains the ionosphere, a region of electrically charged particles (ions) that reflects radio waves back to Earth, enabling long-distance radio transmission. (आयनमंडल — तापमंडल में रेडियो तरंगों का परावर्तन)

 

• The ionosphere extends roughly from 80 km to 400 km above the Earth's surface, largely overlapping with the thermosphere.

 

• This reflective property of the ionosphere allows AM radio and shortwave signals to travel far beyond the horizon by bouncing between the ionosphere and the Earth's surface.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The atmosphere's layers, in order from the Earth's surface outward, are: Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, Thermosphere, Exosphere.

 

• The stratosphere contains the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun.

 

NOTE

 

• Exosphere (Option 1): The outermost layer, merging into space, not involved in radio wave reflection.

 

• Mesosphere (Option 3): The layer where most meteors burn up; it does not reflect radio waves.

 

• Stratosphere (Option 4): Known for the ozone layer and stable flying conditions for aircraft, not radio wave transmission.

question: In Table Tennis, how many lets are allowed in a row on a serve?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Unlimited.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Table Tennis, as per ITTF (International Table Tennis Federation) rules, a "let" occurs when a serve touches the net but still lands correctly in the opponent's court; such a serve is replayed without limit. (लेट — टेबल टेनिस में असीमित बार दोहराया जा सकता है)

 

• There is no restriction on the number of lets that can occur consecutively on serve — each let simply results in a re-serve, regardless of how many times it happens in a row.

 

• This differs from some other racquet sports, where the number of consecutive lets/faults may be restricted.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Table Tennis is governed internationally by the ITTF, headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

 

• A standard game is played to 11 points, and a match typically consists of the best of 5 or 7 games.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (Three, Two, One): These suggest a cap on the number of lets allowed on serve, which is incorrect — ITTF rules impose no such limit.

question: The value of GDP at the current prevailing prices is called _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is nominal GDP.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nominal GDP is the value of all goods and services produced in an economy, calculated using the current prevailing (market) prices of the year in which output is produced. (सांकेतिक/नाममात्र GDP — चालू कीमतों पर)

 

• Because it is not adjusted for inflation, nominal GDP can rise even if actual output stays the same, purely due to a rise in prices.

 

• In contrast, real GDP is calculated using constant (base year) prices, removing the effect of price changes and allowing accurate comparison of output across years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India currently uses 2011–12 as the base year for calculating real GDP and national income estimates.

 

• GDP deflator is the ratio of nominal GDP to real GDP, used as a broad measure of inflation in the economy.

 

NOTE

 

• Current GDP (Option 2): Not a standard formal economic term; often loosely confused with nominal GDP but is not the precise textbook terminology.

 

• Domestic GDP (Option 3): "Domestic" is already inherent in GDP (Gross Domestic Product) and is not the term for current-price valuation.

 

• Real GDP (Option 4): This is GDP valued at constant/base-year prices, the opposite of what the question describes.

question: During which of the following period Ostriches were found in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Palaeolithic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fossil evidence, including ostrich eggshells, found at Upper Palaeolithic sites such as Patne (Maharashtra) and in the Thar Desert (Rajasthan), indicates that ostriches were found in India during the Palaeolithic period. (शुतुरमुर्ग — पुरापाषाण काल में भारत में उपस्थिति)

 

• These findings, dated to around 25,000–40,000 years ago, are significant because ostriches are not native to the Indian subcontinent today, and their presence indicates a very different climate/ecology in prehistoric India.

 

• Decorated ostrich eggshell fragments found at these sites are also considered among the earliest evidence of art/ornamentation in the Indian subcontinent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Palaeolithic (Old Stone) Age in India is broadly divided into Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic phases, based on the type of stone tools used.

 

• The subsequent Mesolithic period is marked by the use of microliths (small stone tools).

 

NOTE

 

• Mesolithic (Option 1): A later Stone Age phase marked by microlithic tools; ostrich fossil evidence in India is primarily associated with the earlier Palaeolithic period.

 

• Chalcolithic (Option 2): The Copper-Stone Age, much later than the period associated with ostrich fossils in India.

 

• Neolithic (Option 3): The New Stone Age, marked by agriculture and settled life, also later than the Palaeolithic ostrich evidence.

question: The Maharashtra Department of Prisons has launched a loan scheme for inmates serving sentences in jails across the state. This credit scheme is titled _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jivhala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Maharashtra Department of Prisons, in association with a bank, launched the "Jivhala" loan scheme to provide credit to inmates serving sentences in jails across the state, in 2022. (जिव्हाळा योजना — महाराष्ट्र कारागृह विभाग)

 

• The scheme was aimed at helping inmates support their families financially and prepare for rehabilitation and reintegration into society after release, by giving them access to formal credit.

 

• It was reportedly first implemented at the Yerwada Central Jail, Pune, before being extended to other jails in Maharashtra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• "Jivhala" is a Marathi word broadly meaning affection/compassion, reflecting the scheme's welfare-oriented objective.

 

• Prison reform initiatives like this aim to reduce the socio-economic vulnerability of inmates' families during incarceration.

 

NOTE

 

• Kishore (Option 2): This name is associated with a Mudra Yojana loan category for small businesses, not the Maharashtra prison credit scheme.

 

• Sukanya (Option 3): Associated with "Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana", a savings scheme for the girl child, unrelated to prison inmates.

 

• Swavlamban (Option 4): Associated with schemes promoting self-reliance/pension in other contexts, not this specific Maharashtra prison credit scheme.

question: In which state is the Maihar court where Baba Allauddin Khan was a musician?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Maihar is a town located in the present-day state of Madhya Pradesh (in Satna district), where the erstwhile princely state's court patronised the legendary musician Baba Allauddin Khan. (मैहर — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• Baba Allauddin Khan served as the court musician of Maihar State and founded the Maihar Gharana, a prominent school of Hindustani classical music.

 

• He was a multi-instrumentalist and teacher (guru) of legendary musicians including Ravi Shankar, Ali Akbar Khan, and Annapurna Devi, and was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Maihar Gharana is distinctive for blending vocal and instrumental (sitar, sarod) music traditions.

 

• Baba Allauddin Khan's compositions and teaching methods significantly shaped modern Hindustani instrumental music.

 

NOTE

 

• Tripura (Option 1), Uttar Pradesh (Option 2) and Chhattisgarh (Option 4): Maihar is not located in any of these states; it lies in the present-day state of Madhya Pradesh.

question: Which company has set up a factory on the banks of river Hugli in 1651?
solution_text:
The correct answer is English.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The English East India Company established a factory (trading post) on the banks of the river Hugli in Bengal in 1651, marking the beginning of its commercial activities in the region. (हुगली नदी — अंग्रेज़ ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी, 1651)

 

• This factory was set up with permission obtained from the Mughal authorities, and it laid the foundation for the later growth of English trade and influence in Bengal.

 

• The English East India Company subsequently expanded its presence in Bengal, eventually establishing Calcutta (Kolkata) as a major trading centre by the end of the 17th century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Portuguese were the first Europeans to establish trading posts in India, with Vasco da Gama arriving at Calicut in 1498.

 

• The French East India Company established its main base at Pondicherry (Puducherry) in 1673.

 

NOTE

 

• Danish (Option 1): The Danish East India Company later set up trading settlements in India, such as at Tranquebar and Serampore, not the 1651 Hugli factory.

 

• Portuguese (Option 2): The Portuguese had established themselves earlier in India (e.g., Goa, Calicut), but the 1651 Hugli factory was set up by the English.

 

• French (Option 4): The French East India Company was formed later (1664) and established its base at Pondicherry, not Hugli in 1651.
